notes: One typescript sheet, with handwritten - 6 - at the top and archive 70 at the lower left. There is no title, date, salutation, signature or separate mathematical display. The body is an opening continuation fragment followed by twenty page-and-line comments, covering pages 18–25. The author asks whether a statement needs another hypothesis on Z; whether linéairement means rationnellement; whether f should be assumed smooth; what hypotheses on X are needed; and whether to give a corollary for NS. The author requests references for the dimension equality, essentially finite type and universally Japanese, and regrets the absence of a proof. These are the author's questions and assertions, not independently established results. The page also proposes spelling and wording corrections. Two left marginal strokes and the detached pair after et are reproduced graphically. H contains only a description, so H is unavailable as a transcription and all h_reading fields are null with diff_h false. Writing state was inspected component by component: body words and reference digits are typed, including their old-style numeral shapes; the Gr arrow and tilde and the marginal strokes are hand-drawn. The two points after et have uncertain authored status; their graphic reproduction does not assert that they are a handwritten colon or that paper discoloration is authored ink. Source images were visually inspected once each in whole/a/b order. Forty-five unique tight crops were inspected once each. The first tool delivery for crops 31–38 was truncated before reaching the reader; those identical retained crops were delivered again in pairs for their first actual inspection, with no recropping. The manifest records two requests but one actual visual inspection for those eight files. No OCR, compilation, web lookup, other page or peer file was used.
math_reading_decisions: All text, accents, endings, punctuation and state changes were independently checked line by line against C in halves a and b. Unmarked C-context targets confirmed: cancelled mis followed by live mis; standard and standart both present; rationnelle and rationelle both present; the later quoted ... is literal; t is recoverable under the first n of donne. The five explicit C doubt places each have a decision row.

The apparent handwritten quality of the reference numerals was inspected at each open reference field. Repeated 2 has the same rounded cap, diagonal and low foot; repeated 3 the same flat cap, diagonal and lower bow; 4 the same tall open left member and crossbar; and 5 the same upper bar and descending rounded lower part. The digit 1 uses the same serifed vertical form as the typewriter l. The fields remain typed; no whole reference has been marked handwritten merely because its numeral design differs from the letter design.

In p.19 li.11 du bas, both Gr terms are typed, with a raised dot on each and a lowered typed top on the second. The intervening handwritten sign has one main shaft, a rightward head with separately visible upper and lower branches, and an independent wavy tilde above. It is retained as \mathrm{Gr}^{\bullet}\handwritten{\xrightarrow{\sim}}\mathrm{Gr}^{\bullet}_{\mathrm{top}}. No second parallel shaft warrants a double arrow.
The spaces after VII and after SGA 5 IV remain unfilled reference spaces. No section number or ellipsis has been supplied in them.

The two dimension expressions have parentheses around Z_s and Z_t, with lowered s then t and an equals sign. They remain \dim(Z_s) = \dim(Z_t). The request for a reference is not a proof of equality, and no independent proof was attempted.

The questions retain Z, X, f and the capital roman NS as on the sheet. Supposer X plat sur S is a proposal in the page comments. The clause N'est-il pas prudent de supposer f lisse retains its question mark.

The final S in each quotation is a typed serifed capital. The first has one separate high apostrophe/prime before the later paired quotation strokes; the last has only the paired closing quotation strokes, with no additional prime. The first remains S' and the final remains S. No final full stop has been added.

The two marginal strokes are visible without enlargement in the b half; the short stroke is rendered with TikZ without counting that wrapper change as a textual difference. The long stroke is separately reported because its overlap with the initial p. is a placement fact.
